subtitulo: The story of a flat search
descripcion: At B2 a story is told with correct time sequencing: past simple for the main events, past perfect for whatever happened earlier. The dramaturgy of a C1 story (a hooked opening, a marked turning point) isn't the focus yet — getting the timeline clear is.

filas: We left early and missed the bus.
We'd already missed the train before we even got there.
It was raining when we arrived.

ejemplos.texto: We left early, but we'd already missed the connection.
It was raining heavily when we finally got there.
First we waited, then we just decided to walk.

notas: The past perfect marks what happened BEFORE the main story timeline — without it, the order of events can be unclear.
First, then, after that structure the story in time without needing extra tenses.
The past continuous is useful for background: what was going on when the main event happened.

contraste.es: Spanish has the pluscuamperfecto with the same logic, so the past perfect transfers easily. Choosing between the Spanish indefinido and pretérito perfecto follows different rules from the English past simple and present perfect, which depend on whether the time period is finished.
contraste.de: German tells spoken stories in the Perfekt, which leads to I have met him yesterday. English stories use the past simple throughout, with the past perfect for earlier events.
contraste.it: Italian tells spoken stories in the passato prossimo, which leads to I have met him yesterday. English stories use the past simple throughout, with the past perfect for earlier events.
contraste.fr: French tells spoken stories in the passé composé, which leads to I have met him yesterday. The written passé simple is a better bridge: like the English past simple, it presents events as a finished sequence.
contraste.pt: Portuguese tells stories in the simple past (encontrei-o ontem), which maps directly onto the English past simple, and tinha + participle onto the past perfect. Storytelling tenses therefore transfer well.

errores: Leaving out the past perfect, which makes the order of events unclear.
Using only the past simple throughout, even for events that happened earlier.
Using first, then and after that in the wrong order.

es: *Resulta que* rendered as *It results that* instead of *It turned out that*.
de: *Auf einmal* rendered as *At once*, which means 'immediately', instead of *Suddenly* or *All of a sudden*.
it: *Succede che* rendered as *It happens that* instead of *It turned out that*.
fr: *Du coup* carried over as *so* in every sentence until it becomes a tic.
pt: *Acontece que* rendered as *It happens that* instead of *It turned out that*.

traducciones.pt: as paredes com pouco isolamento acústico

traducciones.es: Esto fue hace más o menos…

traducciones.fr: Nous étions sur le point de…

redemittel.funcion: highlights what made it worth telling

redemittel.expresion: It all worked out fine in the end.

traducciones.de: Am Ende ist alles gut ausgegangen.
traducciones.it: Alla fine è andato tutto bene.

redemittel.expresion: I've done it differently ever since.

traducciones.pt: Desde então faço de outra maneira.

mision.consigna: Tell the story of how you found (or didn't find) a place to live.
requisitos: clear order: *first, then, after that, in the end*

microtareas.texto: Put your story in five bullet points.
Record 90 seconds of the whole story. Check your tenses.

autochequeo: Is the earlier event marked with the past perfect where needed?
Is the past continuous used for background, not the main events?
Is the time order of the story clear?
Is the story more than just a list of events?
Have I used at least one past perfect correctly?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the time sequencing: past simple, past continuous, past perfect. Check whether earlier events are correctly marked. Do not rewrite the text.
